sections.heading: Most Major Private Insurance Plans Accepted
body: At Des Moines Wellness Center, we believe that financial barriers should never stand in the way of life-saving care. Our admissions team works directly with your provider to maximize your benefits and minimize out-of-pocket costs. We provide a 100% confidential insurance verification process to get you the answers you need in minutes.

sections.heading: What Is Residential Mental Health Treatment?
sections.subheading: Live-in care when weekly appointments are not enough
body: Residential mental health treatment is live-in care. You stay on site and receive structured, daily therapy with 24/7 clinical support, instead of travelling to appointments and going home to the same pressures that made things worse. It suits people whose symptoms are severe, who are not safe or stable at home, or for whom outpatient care simply has not been enough.

At Des Moines Wellness Center, our residential program is built specifically for primary mental health conditions. Psychiatry reviews your medication, therapy runs every day, and the structure of the day does some of the work for you on the days when getting out of bed is the whole task.

Our campus in Johnston, minutes from downtown Des Moines, is designed to be a clinical sanctuary: quiet, private and removed from the noise of everyday life, so your nervous system has the chance to settle while you do the deeper work of getting well.

sections.heading: Mental Health Conditions We Treat
sections.subheading: Intensive, live-in care for depression and a full range of mental health conditions
body: Our residential program provides round-the-clock care for primary mental health conditions, including:

items.title: Depression & Mood Disorders
items.text: Comprehensive residential care for depression, bipolar disorder, and other mood-related conditions through individualized therapy, psychiatric support, and medication management.

items.title: Anxiety & Panic Disorders
items.text: Individualized treatment for generalized anxiety, panic disorder, and social anxiety, helping individuals manage symptoms, develop healthy coping strategies, and regain emotional stability.

items.title: PTSD, Trauma & Dissociative Disorders
items.text: Trauma-informed care for individuals experiencing PTSD, trauma-related conditions, and dissociative disorders, with a focus on emotional regulation, healing, and long-term stability.

items.title: Personality & Schizoaffective Disorders
items.text: Structured therapeutic and psychiatric support for individuals managing personality disorders or schizoaffective disorder, focusing on symptom management, emotional stability, and improved daily functioning.

items.title: Adjustment Disorders & Life Transitions
items.text: Compassionate care for individuals struggling with significant life changes, stressful events, or emotional challenges, helping build resilience and healthier coping skills.

items.title: Non-Acute Eating Disorders
items.text: Therapeutic support for non-acute eating-related concerns associated with mood disorders and emotional distress, addressing underlying mental health challenges and promoting healthier coping strategies.

sections.heading: If you need help right now
body: Call or text 988, the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, to reach a trained counselor free of charge, any time, day or night. If this is a medical emergency, call 911 or go to your nearest emergency room.

sections.heading: Clinical Care Meets Whole-Person Healing
body: We treat the whole person, blending proven clinical therapies with the restorative structure of daily life on campus. Every element of your plan is chosen for you, and adjusted as you progress.

items.title: Individual Therapy
items.text: One-on-one sessions with a master's-level clinician, several times a week, focused on the roots of what you are experiencing.

items.title: Group Therapy
items.text: Small, clinician-led groups where you practice new skills alongside people who understand what you are going through.

items.title: CBT & DBT
items.text: Cognitive behavioral therapy to change the patterns that keep symptoms going, and dialectical behavior therapy for emotional regulation and distress tolerance.

items.title: Trauma-Informed Care & EMDR
items.text: Care delivered with an understanding of how trauma shapes the mind and body, including EMDR where it is clinically indicated.

items.title: Medication Management
items.text: Psychiatric evaluation on admission and ongoing medication review, so adjustments happen in days rather than between distant appointments.

items.title: Family Therapy
items.text: Structured family sessions that repair communication and give the people closest to you the tools to support your recovery.

image.alt: A private therapy room with natural light

sections.heading: A Day in Residential Mental Health Treatment
body: Your days follow a gentle, structured rhythm: individual and group therapy, wellness activities, nourishing meals and quiet time on a calm residential campus. Routine is part of the treatment. When life has felt chaotic or empty, a predictable day gives your mind somewhere steady to stand.

items.title: Mornings: Grounding and Health
items.text: The day starts with a healthy breakfast and a morning check-in with our clinical team, where we review how you slept, how you are feeling and any medication adjustments.

items.title: Afternoons: Clinical Work
items.text: The middle of the day is for one-on-one therapy and small group sessions, where you build the skills to manage symptoms and address what is underneath them.

items.title: Evenings: Reflection and Connection
items.text: After dinner, the pace slows. Peer support groups, wellness activities and personal time for journaling or reading before lights out.

sections.heading: Who Residential Mental Health Treatment Is For
body: Residential care is the right level of support for people who need more than a weekly appointment:

items.title: When outpatient care has not been enough
items.text: If you have been in therapy or on medication and your symptoms are still running your life, a period of intensive, live-in care can reset the trajectory.

items.title: After a crisis or hospitalization
items.text: A structured step between the hospital and home, where stabilization continues with 24/7 support and a clear plan for what comes next.

items.title: When home is part of the problem
items.text: If your environment is full of stress, conflict or triggers, our campus offers a private, secure space to step away and focus entirely on your health.

items.title: When symptoms are disrupting daily life
items.text: If depression, anxiety or trauma symptoms are making it hard to work, sleep, keep up relationships or take care of yourself, round-the-clock structure gives you room to stabilize.

sections.heading: A Calm, Home-Like Setting in Central Iowa
body: Getting well is hard enough; you should not have to do it in a loud, chaotic hospital setting. Our campus in Johnston is designed to be a clinical sanctuary, a quiet, comfortable environment where you can actually hear your own thoughts. By removing the noise and stress of everyday life, we give your nervous system the chance to finally calm down.

You will have a private or semi-private room, healthy meals prepared by our team, quiet rooms and outdoor space for reflection. This is not just about comfort. It is about creating a secure space where you feel safe enough to be honest and do the deep work of recovery.

sections.heading: What Comes After Residential Care
body: Residential treatment is a stage, not the whole journey. As you stabilize, we step your care down gradually so the progress you make on campus holds up at home.

items.title: Residential Mental Health
items.text: Immersive stabilization. Daily therapy and psychiatric care while you live on site in a calm, structured setting.

items.title: Mental Health IOP
items.text: Several therapy sessions a week while you live at home, focused on mental health and built to keep your progress going. Launching soon.

items.title: Outpatient & Virtual Care
items.text: Ongoing therapy and medication management, in person or by secure video, as you return to everyday life.

items.title: A True Environmental Reset

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subheading: Common questions about residential mental health treatment

faqs.q: What is residential mental health treatment?
faqs.a: Residential treatment is live-in care: you stay on site and receive structured therapy with 24/7 clinical support, rather than travelling to appointments. It suits people whose symptoms are severe, or for whom outpatient care has not been enough.

Length of stay is personalized. Your clinical team sets a timeline around your goals and your progress, and reviews it with you as you go rather than fixing it on day one. Most stays range from 30 to 45 days.

faqs.q: What is the difference between inpatient and residential mental health treatment?
faqs.a: The terms are often used interchangeably. Both mean you live on site with round-the-clock support. "Residential" emphasizes our calm, home-like setting rather than a clinical hospital environment.

faqs.q: Can I stay connected with my family?
faqs.a: Yes. We encourage healthy connection in a safe, structured way so you can carry your wellness tools into real life. Our team explains visitation and communication during admissions, and family therapy is part of the program.

faqs.q: What mental health conditions do you treat?
faqs.a: Our residential program treats depression and mood disorders, anxiety and panic disorders, PTSD, trauma and dissociative disorders, personality and schizoaffective disorders, adjustment disorders, and non-acute eating disorders. Our admissions team can talk through your situation and confirm whether residential care is the right fit.

We work with most major private insurance providers as part of the Quadrant Health Network. Because every plan is different, we offer a free, confidential insurance verification before you arrive so you know exactly what is covered. Call us at (888) 378-2158 to get a fast answer.
